prompt: In South Carolina, a driver 21 or older is driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration (DUAC) at what BAC?
explanation: South Carolina law makes it illegal to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more. You can also be charged with DUI at a lower level if your driving is impaired.

prompt: A 19-year-old South Carolina driver is stopped and registers a BAC of 0.02 percent. What happens to the driver's privilege to drive?
choices: It is suspended immediately for at least three months
It is suspended for 30 days only if there was a crash
Nothing, because 0.02 is below the adult limit
A warning letter is mailed to the driver
explanation: Drivers under 21 who register a BAC of 0.02 percent or more have their driving privilege suspended immediately for at least three months. The 0.08 adult limit does not protect them.

prompt: A South Carolina driver under 21 refuses an officer's request to take a test for alcohol. How long, at minimum, will the driver lose driving privileges?
explanation: An under-21 driver who refuses testing immediately loses driving privileges for at least six months, twice the minimum for testing at 0.02 or more.
ref: South Carolina Driver's Manual, p. 38; S.C. Code of Laws § 56-1-286

prompt: What is the alcohol concentration at which a South Carolina driver of a commercial motor vehicle is disqualified from driving a CMV?
explanation: A person driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent or more must be disqualified from driving a CMV, half the 0.08 limit for regular drivers.

prompt: An adult driver with no prior DUI offenses refuses a breath test requested under South Carolina's implied consent law. How long is the license suspension?
explanation: For a first refusal (no prior offenses or suspensions in the past ten years) the suspension is six months. The driver may instead enroll in the Ignition Interlock Device Program for the remaining period.

prompt: A first-time offender in South Carolina takes the breath test and registers 0.16 percent. What administrative license suspension applies?
explanation: Taking the test and registering 0.15 percent or more brings a one-month suspension for a first offender; refusing the test brings six months. Criminal DUI penalties are separate.

prompt: After a first DUI or DUAC conviction in South Carolina, how long must the driver use an ignition interlock device to drive again?
explanation: For a first offense the driver must enroll in the Ignition Interlock Device Program and drive with an interlock for six months. Two years applies to a second offense.

prompt: What is the basic penalty for a first DUI conviction in South Carolina when the driver's BAC was below 0.10 percent?
choices: A $400 fine or 48 hours to 30 days in jail
A $2,100 fine and 5 days in jail
explanation: A first offense is punished by a $400 fine or 48 hours to 30 days in jail (or 48 hours of public service). Penalties rise at BAC 0.10 and 0.16 and for repeat offenses.

prompt: According to the South Carolina Driver's Manual, can you be convicted of impaired driving with a BAC below 0.08?
choices: Only if you are driving a commercial vehicle
Yes, even at 0.05 or a lower BAC combined with drugs
Only if you are involved in a crash
No, 0.08 is the lowest level that counts
explanation: The manual warns you can be convicted of driving impaired even with a BAC of only 0.05, or a lower BAC combined with drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications.

prompt: Under South Carolina law, where may an opened bottle of wine be carried in a car on a public highway?
choices: In the trunk or luggage compartment
In a cup holder if the driver is not drinking
On the floor of the back seat
explanation: It is unlawful to possess beer or wine in an open container in a motor vehicle on a public highway or right of way except in the trunk or luggage compartment.

prompt: A driver's license is suspended for a first DUI committed in 2025. Can the driver get South Carolina's six-month provisional driver's license?
choices: Only if the driver is under 21
Yes, if the BAC was 0.14 or less
No, it is not available for any DUI or DUAC on or after May 19, 2024
explanation: The provisional license is not available for any DUI or DUAC that takes place on or after May 19, 2024. First offenders now use the ignition interlock program instead.

prompt: Under South Carolina's Hands-Free and Distracted Driving Act, which of these is allowed while driving on a public road?
choices: Watching a video call with the phone in a dash mount
Holding your phone on speaker near your mouth
Using an earpiece to talk on a voice call
Reading an email while driving slowly in traffic
explanation: The Act bars holding or supporting a device, reading or sending texts, and watching video. Using an earpiece or a wrist-worn device for voice calls is allowed.

prompt: What is the penalty for a first violation of South Carolina's Hands-Free and Distracted Driving Act?
explanation: A first offense is a $100 fine. Second and later offenses bring a $200 fine and two points on your driving record.

prompt: A South Carolina driver is convicted a second time of violating the hands-free law. What is the penalty?
choices: A $200 fine and two points on the driving record
explanation: Second and subsequent violations bring a $200 fine plus two points on your driving record.

prompt: Who must follow South Carolina's hands-free driving law?
choices: Only drivers with a beginner's permit or restricted license
All drivers operating a motor vehicle on public roads
explanation: The Hands-Free and Distracted Driving Act applies to everyone operating a motor vehicle on any public road in South Carolina, not just teens or new drivers.

prompt: South Carolina has a primary seat belt law. What does that mean?
choices: Belts are required only on highways
Only the driver must wear a belt
An officer can stop you just for an unbelted driver or occupant
You can be ticketed for no belt only after being stopped for another violation
explanation: Under the primary law, an officer with a clear view of an unbelted driver or occupant (or an unrestrained child) may stop the vehicle for that reason alone.

prompt: In South Carolina, a 16-year-old passenger who holds a beginner's permit rides without a seat belt. Who is in violation?
choices: No one, because passengers are exempt
explanation: The driver must make occupants 17 and younger buckle up, except an occupant who has a license, special restricted license or beginner's permit; that occupant is in violation and is fined.

prompt: Under South Carolina law, how must a child under age two ride in a passenger car?
choices: In a rear-facing car seat in a rear seat
In a booster seat with a lap belt
In an adult seat belt if the child is held by an adult
In a forward-facing seat in the front seat
explanation: Children under two must ride in a rear-facing car seat in a rear seat until they exceed the seat maker's height or weight limit.

prompt: When may a South Carolina child ride using only an adult seat belt?
choices: At least age 8 or 57 inches tall, if the belt fits properly
explanation: A child at least 8 years old or at least 57 inches tall may use an adult belt if it fits: lap belt across the thighs and hips, shoulder belt across the chest, and knees bent at the seat edge.

prompt: A 5-year-old in South Carolina has outgrown a forward-facing harness seat but is too small for the adult belt. What is required?
choices: Riding in the front seat with the air bag turned on
No restraint, because the child is over four
A belt-positioning booster seat in a rear seat, used with lap and shoulder belts
explanation: A child at least four who has outgrown the forward-facing seat must ride in a booster seat in a rear seat until the adult belt fits; the booster must be used with both lap and shoulder belts, never a lap belt alone.

prompt: What is the minimum age to get a regular (Class D) beginner's permit in South Carolina?
explanation: You must be at least 15 and pass the vision and knowledge tests to get a beginner's permit. Applicants under 18 need a qualified adult to sign consent.

prompt: A 16-year-old with no driving experience gets a South Carolina beginner's permit. How long must the permit be held before applying for a license?
explanation: Drivers 17 and younger must hold the beginner's permit at least 180 days; they may apply on the 181st day.

prompt: A 22-year-old gets a first South Carolina beginner's permit. When may this driver apply for a driver's license?
choices: After holding the permit at least 180 days
Immediately, because adults are exempt from the permit
After holding the permit at least 30 days
explanation: Drivers 18 and older must hold the beginner's permit at least 30 days and may apply on the 31st day. The 180-day rule applies to drivers 17 and younger.

prompt: Who may supervise a South Carolina beginner's permit holder driving at 4 p.m.?
choices: A licensed driver at least 18 in any seat
A licensed driver at least 21 with at least one year of driving experience in the front seat
Any adult over 25, licensed or not
explanation: From 6 a.m. to midnight, the supervisor must be a licensed driver at least 21 years old with at least one year of driving experience, seated in the front seat.

prompt: May a South Carolina beginner's permit holder drive between midnight and 6 a.m.?
choices: Yes, with any licensed driver 21 or older
Yes, but only with a qualified individual such as a parent or legal guardian listed in state law
Yes, alone if returning from work
explanation: After midnight, a permit holder may drive only when supervised by a licensed individual listed in SC Code 56-1-100(A)(1-7), such as a parent, legal guardian or other qualified adult.

prompt: How many hours of supervised practice driving must a 15- or 16-year-old complete before applying for a South Carolina license?
explanation: Teens who are 15 or 16 must practice at least 40 hours, including ten hours of night driving, with a parent, guardian or other qualified adult.

prompt: What driver education must a 15- or 16-year-old complete for a first South Carolina license?
choices: 30 hours in the classroom and 6 hours driving
8 hours in the classroom and 6 hours driving
explanation: A 15- or 16-year-old applicant must complete driver's education of eight hours in the classroom and six hours driving, and be enrolled in school with satisfactory attendance.

prompt: At what age can a South Carolina teen who meets all requirements get a conditional license?
explanation: A conditional license is available to teens at least 15 1/2 but under 16 who meet the permit, education and practice requirements and pass the vision and skills tests.

prompt: In South Carolina, a 16-year-old (under 17) who meets the requirements and passes the vision and skills tests gets which license?
choices: A regular license with full privileges
explanation: Drivers who are 16 but under 17 receive a special restricted license, which has the same night and passenger limits as the conditional license.

prompt: During standard time, when may a South Carolina conditional or special restricted license holder drive alone?
explanation: These teens may drive alone from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. (8 p.m. during daylight saving time). From then until midnight they need a licensed driver at least 21 with them.

prompt: It is July (daylight saving time). Until what time may a South Carolina special restricted license holder drive without a supervising adult?
explanation: The unsupervised window ends at 6 p.m., extended to 8 p.m. during daylight saving time.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a special restricted license wants to drive at 10 p.m. Which is required?
choices: A note from a parent kept in the car
Nothing; the restriction ends at 9 p.m.
A licensed driver who is at least 21 in the vehicle
Any licensed passenger who is at least 18
explanation: From 6 p.m. (8 p.m. in daylight saving time) to midnight, a conditional or special restricted driver must be with a licensed driver who is at least 21.

prompt: How many passengers under 21 may a South Carolina conditional or special restricted license holder carry when no licensed adult 21 or older is present?
explanation: No more than two passengers under 21 are allowed unless a licensed adult at least 21 is in the vehicle. Transporting family members or students to and from school is the only exception.

prompt: A South Carolina teen with a special restricted license drives four younger siblings to school with no adult. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, transporting family members or students to and from school is an exception
Only if a parent signs a form each day
No, the limit is two passengers under 21 in all cases
explanation: The two-passenger limit has one exception: transporting family members or students to and from school.

prompt: What does a South Carolina special restricted license with a waiver allow?
choices: Driving alone until midnight for work or certain activities
explanation: The waiver lets a 16-year-old drive alone until midnight for work or certain extracurricular activities. It never allows driving after midnight. The new license costs $25.

prompt: When does a South Carolina teen driver earn full driving privileges?
choices: When the teen finishes high school
At 17, or after one year on a conditional or special restricted license with no traffic offenses or at-fault collisions
After six months on any restricted license
explanation: Full privileges come at 17, or after keeping a conditional or special restricted license for one year with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collisions. The SCDMV mails a sleeve to wrap around the license.

prompt: A 16-year-old South Carolina driver gets six points within the first year of holding a license. What happens?
choices: The license is suspended for six months
The points are cut in half
The driver must retake the knowledge test
explanation: A driver under 17 who gets six or more points before holding the license for one year has the license suspended for six months.

prompt: A South Carolina beginner's permit holder accumulates six points. Can a defensive driving course stop the excessive-points suspension?
choices: No, the course will not reinstate an excessive-points suspension
No suspension applies to permit holders
Yes, any defensive driving course cancels it
Yes, if completed online within 30 days
explanation: Permit, conditional and special restricted holders with six or more points are suspended for excessive points, and completing a defensive driving course will not reinstate that suspension.

prompt: For a South Carolina driver 17 or older, how many points lead to a license suspension?
explanation: Drivers 17 and older get a warning letter at six points; reaching 12 or more points results in suspension.

prompt: In June a South Carolina driver gets 4 points for a violation. If nothing else happens, how many points from that ticket remain the next June?
explanation: Points are reduced by half one year after the violation date, so 4 points become 2 points.

prompt: How often may a South Carolina driver use a defensive driving course to reduce points?
explanation: A point reduction may be made only once in a three-year period. The 8-hour classroom course must be taken in SC (not online) after the violation date.

prompt: Which statement about South Carolina's point-reduction defensive driving course is true?
choices: It must be eight hours of classroom training taken in SC
It can be taken before the violation to bank credit
It cancels a suspension that has already begun
explanation: The course cannot be done online, must be taken in SC as eight hours of classroom training after the violation date, and will not cancel a suspension that has already started.

prompt: How many points does South Carolina assess for speeding no more than 10 mph over the posted limit?
explanation: Speeding up to 10 mph over is 2 points; more than 10 but less than 25 over is 4 points; 25 mph or more over is 6 points.

prompt: A South Carolina driver is convicted of going 27 mph over the posted speed limit. How many points are added?
explanation: Speeding 25 mph or more above the posted limit carries 6 points, the same as reckless driving.

prompt: How many points does South Carolina assess for passing a stopped school bus?
explanation: Passing a stopped school bus is a 6-point violation in South Carolina, the same as reckless driving.

prompt: What are South Carolina's minimum liability insurance limits?
explanation: Policies must cover at least $25,000 for bodily injury to one person, $50,000 for injury to two or more people in one accident, and $25,000 for property damage.

prompt: Besides liability coverage, what must every South Carolina auto insurance policy include?
explanation: South Carolina policies must include an uninsured motorist provision with limits no less than the 25/50/25 liability minimums.

prompt: Which documents must you have with you when driving in South Carolina?
choices: Your license and a vehicle inspection sticker
Your license, vehicle registration and valid insurance card
explanation: You must carry a valid driver's license, vehicle registration and a valid insurance card for the vehicle class you are driving, or you may be fined.

prompt: You move to South Carolina permanently with a valid license from another state. How soon must you apply for an SC license?
explanation: New permanent residents must apply for an SC license or ID within 45 days (active-duty military and U.S. government employees are excepted) and turn in the out-of-state license.

prompt: A new South Carolina resident's out-of-state license expired 11 months ago. What must the driver do to get an SC license?
choices: Pass the knowledge, skills and vision tests
Wait until the old license is renewed in the other state
explanation: If an out-of-state license has been expired for more than nine months, you must pass the knowledge, skills and vision tests before getting an SC license.

prompt: Which driver may NOT renew a South Carolina license online?
choices: A driver whose license expired one month ago
A driver with a vision certificate sent by an SC eye doctor
A U.S. citizen with a Class D license
A driver who received more than five points in the last two years
explanation: Online renewal requires, among other things, no more than five points in the last two years, a license not expired more than nine months, and an electronically submitted vision certificate.

prompt: You fail the South Carolina skills (road) test for the first time. How long must you wait to retest?
explanation: After a first failure you wait two business days; after a second, seven calendar days; after a third or more, 30 calendar days, regardless of age.

prompt: What happens if you do not wear your seat belt during a South Carolina skills test?
choices: Points are deducted but you can still pass
explanation: The manual states you will automatically fail the skills test if you do not use your seat belt.

prompt: What is the minimum vision standard for a South Carolina non-commercial license?
explanation: The minimum standard does not require better than 20/40 corrected in one eye. If you need glasses or contacts to meet it, a restriction is added and you must wear them to drive.

prompt: To drive a golf cart on public roads in South Carolina, how old must you be?
choices: At least 18 with a valid driver's license
At least 16 with a valid driver's license
explanation: You must be at least 16 and have a valid driver's license. The cart needs an SCDMV permit decal and may be driven in daytime within four miles of its registered address.

prompt: A South Carolina driver gets a traffic ticket. Is the driver required to sign it?
choices: Yes, or the driver will be arrested
No, South Carolina does not require a driver to sign a traffic ticket
Only if the driver is under 18
explanation: In SC a driver is not required to sign a traffic ticket, and accepting one is not an admission of guilt. Other states may arrest a driver who refuses to sign.

prompt: Which test is NOT required to get a South Carolina moped (Class G) license?
explanation: A moped license requires passing the vision and knowledge tests only; the SCDMV does not require a skills test for a moped license. The minimum age is 15.

prompt: Unless a different limit is posted, what is the maximum speed in a South Carolina urban district (a built-up business or residential area)?
explanation: Thirty miles an hour is the maximum speed in an urban district unless signs show otherwise. Local authorities may set a lower limit after an engineering study.

prompt: What is the highest speed limit allowed on South Carolina interstate highways where posted?
explanation: State law sets 70 mph as the maximum on interstates and other freeways where signs give notice of that limit.

prompt: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on an unpaved road in South Carolina?
explanation: Highways outside urban districts are generally limited to 55 mph, but unpaved roads are limited to 40 mph.

prompt: If no other limit is posted, what is the maximum speed on a paved South Carolina highway outside an urban district that is not an interstate or posted multilane divided highway?
explanation: The default limit in other locations is 55 mph. Interstates may be posted at 70 and multilane divided primary highways at 60.

prompt: What minimum following distance does the South Carolina Driver's Manual recommend in normal conditions?
explanation: The manual says always try to keep a minimum following distance of 4 seconds. If you pass the fixed point before counting 'one thousand four,' you are too close.

prompt: You are driving at night on a road you do not know. Per the South Carolina Driver's Manual, how should you change your following distance?
choices: Cut it to 3 seconds so you can follow the taillights ahead
Add one second, the same as for any night driving
explanation: The manual says to add at least one second for night driving and at least two additional seconds when driving on unfamiliar roads at night.

prompt: South Carolina's speed limits are 'maximum lawful speeds.' What else does state law require?
choices: Speed limits apply only in good weather
You may always drive at the limit
Never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for the conditions
You may exceed the limit by 5 mph when passing
explanation: Under the basic speed rule, you may not drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for actual and potential hazards, even if that is below the posted limit.

prompt: Under South Carolina law, when is driving very slowly illegal?
choices: When it impedes the normal and reasonable movement of traffic without a safety reason
Only on roads posted 55 mph or more
Only when someone honks at you
explanation: No one may drive so slowly that it impedes the normal and reasonable movement of traffic, unless reduced speed is needed for safety or required by law.

prompt: In South Carolina, may you turn right on a steady red light?
choices: Yes, after stopping, unless a sign prohibits it, yielding to pedestrians and traffic
Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
Only when a green arrow is also shown
explanation: A right turn on red is allowed unless a sign prohibits it. Stop before the crosswalk first and yield to pedestrians and other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

prompt: When is a left turn on a steady red light allowed in South Carolina?
choices: From a two-way street onto a two-way street when clear
From any street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping, unless a sign prohibits it
explanation: Unless a sign prohibits it, after stopping you may turn left on red only from a one-way street into a one-way street, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

prompt: How far ahead must you signal before turning, changing lanes or merging in South Carolina?
explanation: It is state law to signal 100 feet or more before changing lanes, turning, or merging into traffic. Cancel the signal when done.

prompt: On a South Carolina controlled-access highway such as an interstate, when may you drive in the far-left lane?
choices: Any time you are at the speed limit
Generally only when overtaking and passing another vehicle
explanation: South Carolina law bars driving in the farthest left lane of a controlled-access highway except to overtake and pass, with limited exceptions such as heavy congestion or bad weather.

prompt: Which situation is an exception to South Carolina's left-lane law on controlled-access highways?
choices: No other vehicle is directly behind you in the left lane
Your exit is on the right in 10 miles
You are listening to navigation directions
You are going exactly the speed limit
explanation: Exceptions include no vehicle directly behind you, congestion, snow or bad weather, right-lane hazards, a left-side exit, and emergency or highway work vehicles.

prompt: What does the South Carolina Driver's Manual say about the zipper (late) merge when traffic backs up before a closed lane?
choices: It is allowed only for trucks
It is not required by law, but it is a best practice
explanation: Law does not require the zipper merge, but the manual calls it a best practice in heavy, slow traffic: use both lanes to the merge point and take turns.

prompt: In South Carolina, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
explanation: You may not stand or park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, except momentarily to pick up or drop off passengers.

prompt: In South Carolina, you may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
explanation: Standing or parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection is prohibited, and you may not stop on the crosswalk itself.

prompt: You want to park on the approach to a stop sign at the side of a South Carolina road. How far away must you be?
explanation: Do not stand or park within 30 feet on the approach to a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal at the side of the road.

prompt: In South Carolina, how close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park?
explanation: Parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing is prohibited, except while actually loading or unloading.

prompt: In South Carolina, where may you NOT stand or park near a fire station?
choices: Within 20 feet of its driveway entrance, or within 75 feet of the entrance across the street when signposted
explanation: The law bars standing or parking within 20 feet of a fire station driveway entrance, and within 75 feet of the entrance on the opposite side of the street when properly signposted.

prompt: When parallel parking next to a curb in South Carolina, how far from the curb may your wheels be?
explanation: Do not park more than 18 inches from the curb or edge of the pavement.

prompt: You are driving on a two-lane road in South Carolina and meet a school bus stopped with red lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Stop, whichever direction you are traveling
Stop only if you are behind the bus
Stop only if children are visible
Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully
explanation: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus and stay stopped until the bus moves or its red lights stop flashing.

prompt: You are traveling in the opposite direction from a stopped school bus on a South Carolina highway with two lanes in each direction. Must you stop?
choices: Only if there is no median
Only if the stop arm is extended
No, opposite-direction traffic need not stop on a multi-lane highway
explanation: Drivers meeting a stopped school bus on a multi-lane highway (four lanes, at least two in each direction) need not stop. Drivers behind the bus must always stop.

prompt: You are behind a school bus that stops with red lights flashing on a four-lane South Carolina highway. What must you do?
choices: Change lanes and slow to 25 mph
Stop and wait until the bus moves or the red lights stop flashing
Stop only if children are crossing
explanation: You must always stop on any highway when you are behind the bus, and not proceed until it moves or its red lights stop flashing.

prompt: A school bus ahead of you in South Carolina has its amber (yellow) warning lights flashing. What does the law say?
choices: You must not overtake the bus
Amber lights apply only to oncoming traffic
You may pass on the right
explanation: Amber lights mean the bus is preparing to stop; South Carolina law prohibits overtaking a school bus with its amber signals on.

prompt: An ambulance with siren and flashing lights approaches you on a two-lane South Carolina road. What should you do?
choices: Pull to the right edge of the road clear of intersections, stop, and wait until it passes
Speed up to clear the way
explanation: Yield by pulling to a position parallel and close to the right edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

prompt: In South Carolina, how close may you follow a fire truck that is responding to an emergency?
explanation: Unless on official business, you may not follow a responding fire apparatus closer than 500 feet, or stop within 500 feet of one stopped at an emergency.

prompt: You approach a stopped police car with flashing lights on a South Carolina four-lane highway. What does the move-over law require?
choices: Slow down and move to a lane away from the emergency vehicle if it is safe
explanation: Slow down and change into a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle if safety and traffic allow. If a lane change is unsafe, slow down and proceed with caution.

prompt: You cannot safely change lanes when passing a stopped tow truck with flashing lights in South Carolina. What must you do?
choices: Stop in your lane until it leaves
Slow down and proceed with caution at a safe speed
Nothing; the law covers only police cars
explanation: If a lane change is unsafe, slow down and proceed with caution. Tow and recovery vehicles responding to an incident count as authorized emergency vehicles under the move-over law.
ref: South Carolina Driver's Manual, pp. 123-124; S.C. Code of Laws § 56-5-1538

prompt: A railroad crossing signal starts flashing as you approach in South Carolina. Where must you stop?
choices: Between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail
At least 100 feet from the tracks
Anywhere, as long as you do not touch the tracks
explanation: Stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, and do not go until it is safe. Never drive around or under a lowered gate.

prompt: How much space does South Carolina law require you to give a bicycle when you pass?
choices: No space; bicycles must move to the shoulder
A safe operating distance at all times; the manual says slow down and give as much space as possible
explanation: South Carolina requires drivers to keep a safe operating distance from bicycles at all times. The manual adds: slow down, allow as much space as possible, and consider the bicyclist's speed.

prompt: A bicyclist in South Carolina is stopped at a red light that does not change. When may the rider legally go through?
choices: Never; the rider must wait for green
After stopping for 120 seconds, then treating the light like a stop sign and going only when safe
Immediately, because bicycles may ignore signals
explanation: South Carolina lets bicyclists, motorcyclists and moped drivers proceed on a steady red after a full stop of 120 seconds, using due care and treating the signal like a stop sign.

prompt: When following a motorcycle in South Carolina, what minimum following distance does the manual recommend?
choices: 4 seconds, or more in wet conditions
explanation: Allow at least a 4-second following distance behind a motorcycle, and more on wet roads, because riders may suddenly change speed or position to avoid hazards.

prompt: When does South Carolina law require your headlights to be on?
choices: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and when wipers are needed for rain, sleet or snow
Only when it is completely dark
From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
explanation: Lights must be on from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, whenever wipers are in use because of rain, sleet or snow, and when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Parking lights alone do not count.

prompt: It is mid-afternoon and rain has you running your wipers steadily in South Carolina. What must you do with your headlights?
explanation: South Carolina requires headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use because of rain, sleet or snow (intermittent wiper use in a light mist is excepted). Parking lights alone do not satisfy the law.

prompt: When must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle in South Carolina?
explanation: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.
ref: South Carolina Driver's Manual, p. 126; S.C. Code of Laws § 56-5-4780

prompt: When following another vehicle at night in South Carolina, within what distance must you use low beams?
explanation: Use low beams when following another vehicle that is less than 200 feet ahead of you.

prompt: How many points does South Carolina assess for endangering a highway worker when no one is injured?
explanation: Endangering a highway worker is 2 points with no injury and 4 points if an injury results, plus fines.

prompt: A South Carolina road marker reads 'S-40-123.' What does the first number after the 'S' tell you?
choices: The number of the county the road is in
explanation: Secondary system road markers show the county number first after the letter 'S,' then the road number. Each county has its own set of secondary road numbers.

prompt: In South Carolina, what does a Hurricane Evacuation Route sign mark?
choices: A road where speed limits are suspended
A road used as an evacuation route when a mandatory evacuation is declared for the coast
explanation: During a hurricane, a mandatory evacuation may be declared for SC's coastal areas; the evacuation route sign shows roads used for that evacuation.

prompt: You are in a South Carolina crash in which someone is injured. Whom must you notify immediately?
choices: The local police, county sheriff, or Highway Patrol, by the quickest means
No one if the injury is minor
explanation: The driver in a crash with injury or death must immediately notify the local police (in a city) or the county sheriff or nearest Highway Patrol office.

prompt: Your South Carolina crash caused about $1,500 in damage and no officer investigated it. What must the driver or owner do?
choices: Send a written report with proof of insurance to the SCDMV within 15 days
Report it within 30 days to the insurance company only
Nothing, if no one was hurt
explanation: If a crash with injury, death or apparent damage of $1,000 or more was not investigated by police, the operator or owner must send a written report and insurance verification to the SCDMV within 15 days.

prompt: You are pulled over in South Carolina and have a firearm in the vehicle. What does the manual tell you to do?
choices: Get out and place it on the hood
Hand the weapon to the officer
Inform the officer of all weapons upon first contact
explanation: Inform the officer of all weapons in the vehicle at first contact; concealed weapons permit holders should follow CWP procedures. Keep your hands visible.

prompt: Who must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle in South Carolina?
explanation: South Carolina requires motorcycle operators and passengers under 21 to wear approved helmets at all times. Riders 21 and older are not required by law to wear one, though helmets are strongly recommended.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 18

prompt: A helmet worn by a South Carolina rider under 21 must have which features?
choices: A full face shield and bright color
A neck or chin strap and reflectorizing on both sides
explanation: The required helmet must be an approved type with either a neck or chin strap, and it must be reflectorized on both sides.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 18

prompt: What eye protection does South Carolina law require for motorcycle operators under 21?
explanation: SC requires operators under 21 to wear goggles or a face shield in addition to a helmet.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 19

prompt: Is lane splitting (riding between lanes or rows of vehicles) legal in South Carolina?
explanation: South Carolina prohibits operating a motorcycle between lanes of traffic or between adjacent lines or rows of vehicles (police on duty excepted).
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 20

prompt: How many motorcycles may ride side by side in a single lane in South Carolina?
choices: Any number if traffic is light
explanation: Motorcycles may not be operated more than two abreast in a single lane.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 20

prompt: Under South Carolina's 'two minute law,' when may a motorcyclist go through a steady red light?
choices: After a full stop of 120 seconds, treating the light as a stop sign and proceeding only when safe
After 30 seconds if no cars are present
explanation: If a signal does not change, a motorcyclist may proceed on a steady red only after a full and complete stop of 120 seconds (two minutes), using due care and treating the signal as a stop sign.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 20

prompt: When must a motorcycle's headlight be on in South Carolina?
choices: Whenever the motorcycle is operated on public streets or highways
explanation: When operating a motorcycle on public streets or highways, you must have the headlight turned on and burning.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 19

prompt: With a South Carolina Class M beginner's permit, when may you ride alone during daylight saving time?
explanation: A motorcycle permit holder may ride alone from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., or until 8 p.m. during daylight saving time. Other hours require supervision.

prompt: Who may supervise a South Carolina motorcycle permit holder riding at night?
choices: No one; permit holders may not ride at night at all
Any licensed car driver riding as a passenger
A motorcycle-licensed driver at least 21 with at least one year of experience, within a safe viewing distance
explanation: At night the permit holder must be accompanied by a motorcycle-licensed driver at least 21 with at least one year of driving experience, who stays within a safe viewing distance.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 9

prompt: A South Carolina motorcycle permit holder fails the motorcycle skills test at an SCDMV branch three times. What must happen next?
choices: Wait 30 days and retest at the branch
Complete an SCDMV-authorized motorcycle safety course and retake the test as part of the course
Get a new permit and start over
explanation: After three or more failures at a branch, you must complete an SCDMV-authorized motorcycle safety course and retest as part of the course; you may not test again at a branch office.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 9

prompt: Under South Carolina law, where is it illegal to stop, stand or park even for a moment, unless needed to avoid traffic or directed by police?
choices: Beside a fire hydrant while a passenger gets out
On a street with no curb
explanation: South Carolina prohibits stopping, standing or parking within an intersection except to avoid conflict with traffic or when directed by police or a traffic-control device. Near a fire hydrant, the 15-foot rule allows stopping momentarily to pick up or drop off passengers.

prompt: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian is still crossing in the intersection in front of you in South Carolina. What must you do?
choices: Go, because the green light gives you the right-of-way
Yield to the pedestrian until the way is clear
explanation: The South Carolina Driver's Manual says you must yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians in the intersection even if the traffic light is green.

prompt: In South Carolina, a pedestrian guided by a dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street ahead. What must you do?
choices: Slow down and steer around the pedestrian
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian
Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk
explanation: You must always yield to people who are visually impaired; when a pedestrian guided by a dog or carrying a white cane is crossing, you must come to a complete stop. The manual also says not to use your horn near blind pedestrians.

prompt: Your phone is in a dash mount while you drive in South Carolina. Under the Hands-Free and Distracted Driving Act, which is still illegal?
choices: Using a voice command through an earpiece
Reading a text message on the mounted screen
Talking on a call through a wrist-worn device
explanation: Even if you are not holding the phone, South Carolina bars all drivers from reading, writing or sending any form of text, including messages, emails, app interactions and website information. Earpieces and wrist-worn devices for voice communication are allowed.

prompt: Besides two-wheel motorcycles, what else may you operate with a South Carolina Class M license?
choices: Cars and light trucks, as with a Class D license
Nothing else; mopeds need their own Class G license
Only scooters, but not mopeds or three-wheelers
explanation: A Class M license is required to ride a motorcycle, or a motorcycle with a detachable sidecar, on public roads, and with it you may also operate a moped or a three-wheel motorcycle. It does not cover cars; a moped (Class G) license is only needed if you hold no higher-class license.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, pp. 10-11

prompt: Your BAC is below 0.08, but alcohol has affected your riding. According to the South Carolina motorcycle manual, which is true?
choices: You cannot be charged at all, since you are under 0.08
You can be charged only if you are also speeding
You can still be impaired and convicted of riding impaired
Only riders under 21 can be charged below 0.08
explanation: Impairment begins with the first drink, so even under 0.08 you can be impaired and convicted for riding impaired, and your license and riding privileges may be suspended. Riders under 21 can have their license automatically suspended at a BAC of 0.02 or higher.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, pp. 17, 24

prompt: A South Carolina motorcycle rider is 21 or older. At what BAC is the rider considered intoxicated?
explanation: An adult rider with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered intoxicated, and South Carolina law makes riding with 0.08 or more an unlawful alcohol concentration. Impairment starts well below that. Riders under 21 can lose their license at 0.02, and adults at 0.15 or higher can have their license automatically suspended.
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, pp. 17, 24; S.C. Code of Laws § 56-5-2933

prompt: According to South Carolina's motorcycle manual, how should three-wheel vehicles ride when traveling in a group?
choices: Single file, at least four seconds apart
Side by side, two vehicles to a lane
Single file, about one car length apart
explanation: Three-wheel vehicles are nearly as wide as some cars, so they can't use a staggered formation. South Carolina's manual says to ride single file and keep a safe margin of at least four seconds between vehicles. (The MSF manual's minimum is two seconds.)
ref: South Carolina Motorcycle and Moped Operator Manual, p. 95
